spec.cue: Colour is gone, detail is fairly fine and the field is very wide.

fov.note: the middle between one cuttlefish eye at 253 degrees and a young squid at 311 degrees; the blend is the app's

cpd.note: cuttlefish are put at about 8; an octopus tested at 12 and a squid at 6.6 bracket it; one value for the whole group is the app's

topoS.note: the records describe a sharper horizontal stripe across the retina but give no ratio; the strength is the app's

sat.note: most cephalopods have one visual pigment and are colour blind; the mapping to a grey picture is the app's

pupil.note: an octopus pupil closes to a horizontal slit in bright light; the records describe octopus only, so other cephalopods keep the person's pupil

rows: A behavioural test gave an octopus about 12 cycles per degree, and a lens test on a squid gave about 6.6. A person has about 30. Cuttlefish are put near 8. A squid just after hatching manages only 0.63. The picture is blurred to 8 for the whole group.
Most octopus, squid and cuttlefish have a single visual pigment, with its peak between 470 and 500 nanometres. Tests on octopus and cuttlefish found no colour vision. The picture is drawn in grey.

One cuttlefish eye covers 253 degrees along the horizontal, and a young oval squid reaches 311 degrees at seven days old. A cuttlefish has about 86 degrees of overlap between its eyes at the front, and up to 75 degrees when it hunts.
An octopus pupil is round in darkness and closes to a horizontal slit in bright light. The slit appears in the first weeks after the young settle on the bottom.
An octopus has its most densely packed light receptors in a central horizontal stripe. A cuttlefish has a visual equator of high receptor density, set a little above the middle of the eye.
A squid follows flicker up to about 51 flashes a second. An octopus reaches 72 in very bright light and only 20 when the light is dim. A cuttlefish is put at 30. The picture keeps a person's pace.
An octopus can tell the plane of polarized light apart, and one test found a very small threshold. The picture leaves this out for now.

The field of 282 degrees, the single sharpness of 8 cycles per degree, the grey picture, the strength of the sharper middle stripe and the horizontal slit for octopus are the app's own settings, set inside the measured range.

claims.how: 282 lies at the middle of 253 degrees for one cuttlefish eye and 311 degrees for a young squid.
The cuttlefish acuity record states about 8 cycles per degree.
The records say most cephalopods are colour blind with one visual pigment, which the app maps to a saturation of 0.
The octopus record says the pupil constricts to a horizontal slit in bright light.

quotes.quote: The uniocular visual field was found to be 253° on the horizontal plane
the cuttlefish visual acuity is approximately 8 cycles per degree
the vast majority of cephalopod species are color blind, possessing only a single visual pigment
in bright light, it constricts to a horizontal slit
